description: vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor triggered by a specific login string, allowing remote command execution.
FTP service exposed; credentials and data are transmitted in cleartext unless FTPS/SFTP is enforced.
Telnet is enabled; all traffic including credentials is unencrypted and susceptible to interception.
OpenSSH 7.2 is affected by a user enumeration vulnerability via timing differences during authentication.
SMTP service exposed to the network; verify open-relay configuration and enforce STARTTLS.
SMBv1 (port 445) may be vulnerable to the EternalBlue remote code execution exploit if unpatched.
NetBIOS session service exposed; can leak host/share information and enable enumeration attacks.
MySQL 5.5.x authentication bypass allowing repeated password guesses to eventually succeed due to a memcmp flaw.
Database service exposed directly to the network; should be restricted to application-tier hosts only.
RDP service exposed; if unpatched, vulnerable to BlueKeep pre-authentication remote code execution.
VNC service exposed; often configured with weak or no authentication, risking full remote desktop takeover.
Apache 2.2.x is vulnerable to the 'Range header' denial-of-service attack.
Unencrypted HTTP service exposed; consider redirecting to HTTPS.
HTTPS service exposed; confirm TLS configuration disables deprecated protocol versions and weak ciphers.
Samba 3.0.20 through 3.0.25rc3 'username map script' allows remote command execution via shell metacharacters in the username field (the classic Metasploitable2 'usermap_script' exploit).
Java RMI Registry default configuration allows unauthenticated remote class loading, frequently leading to remote code execution.
Port 1524 is answering with a root shell backdoor (the classic Metasploitable2 'ingreslock' backdoor left over from a prior compromise) -- any connection to this port grants immediate root access.
NFS service exposed to the network; misconfigured exports can allow unauthorized mounting and read/write access to shared filesystems.
distccd allows arbitrary command execution via crafted compilation jobs when exposed without access controls, as bundled (misconfigured) in Metasploitable2.
PostgreSQL exposed to the network; verify pg_hba.conf restricts access and default/weak credentials (e.g. postgres/postgres) are not in use.
X11 server exposed to the network; if access control is disabled (xhost +), this allows remote keystroke capture and screen access.
UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 contains a trojaned backdoor allowing arbitrary remote command execution via a crafted IRC message.
Apache Tomcat manager application exposed; default/weak credentials (e.g. tomcat/tomcat) commonly allow WAR file upload and remote code execution.
rexec (port 512) authenticates in cleartext and is considered a legacy, insecure remote execution protocol.
rlogin (port 513) can permit passwordless login from trusted hosts via .rhosts configuration -- a classic legacy trust-based attack vector.
rsh (port 514) transmits commands and data in cleartext and, like rlogin, is often configured with weak host-based trust.
rpcbind exposure can be leveraged for UDP amplification denial-of-service attacks.
POP3 service exposed without TLS wrapper (use POP3S / port 995 instead).

Redis exposed without authentication is a well-known cloud misconfiguration; an unauthenticated instance allows full read/write access and, on Debian-based builds, a Lua sandbox escape (CVE-2022-0543) enabling remote code execution.
MongoDB exposed without authentication (the historical default) allows any network client to read, modify, or delete all data -- one of the most common causes of real-world data breaches.
Elasticsearch exposed without authentication allows full read/write access to all indexed data via its REST API, and has been a frequent source of large-scale data leaks.
Memcached exposed to the network (especially over UDP) can be abused for massive DDoS reflection/amplification attacks and may leak cached application data.

An unauthenticated Docker Engine API (plain HTTP, no TLS) grants full control of the host: an attacker can launch a privileged container mounting the host filesystem, resulting in complete host compromise.
Jenkins' built-in CLI command parser is vulnerable to an arbitrary file-read flaw that can be leveraged for remote code execution when the CLI endpoint is reachable without authentication.

An exposed phpMyAdmin interface, especially with default or weak credentials, grants direct access to underlying databases and, via features like LOAD_FILE or log poisoning, can lead to remote code execution.
Grafana versions affected by the plugin path-traversal vulnerability allow unauthenticated arbitrary file read from the server's filesystem.
An exposed Prometheus web UI/API with no authentication can leak internal service topology, metrics, and configuration details useful for reconnaissance.
SNMP responding with the default 'public' community string allows unauthenticated read (and sometimes write) access to detailed device configuration and network topology information.
Heartbleed: affected OpenSSL 1.0.1 branches leak up to 64KB of process memory per request, potentially exposing private keys, session tokens, and credentials.
Shellshock: a crafted environment variable processed by a vulnerable Bash via CGI can achieve remote code execution on affected Apache/CGI configurations.
WordPress's XML-RPC endpoint (xmlrpc.php), when enabled, is commonly abused for credential brute-forcing (via system.multicall amplification) and pingback-based SSRF/DDoS.
An exposed .git directory or git daemon protocol port can allow an attacker to reconstruct full source history, potentially recovering hardcoded credentials or proprietary code.
Apache CouchDB's Erlang-based JSON parser discrepancy allows an authentication bypass that can be chained to CVE-2017-12636 for remote code execution.
